title: Julia Child-Inspired Glazed Pearl Onions with Demi-Glace
description: Tender pearl onions browned in butter, braised with beef demi-glace and herbs, and reduced to a rich, glossy glaze. A red wine vinegar finish balances the richness if needed.
totalTime: About 1 hour with peeled onions; about 1 hour 20 minutes if peeling
ingredients: 454 g (1 lb) peeled pearl onions, preferably fresh
15 g (1 tbsp) unsalted butter, for browning
10–12 g More Than Gourmet Demi-Glace Gold concentrate (not pre-diluted)
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
5–10 g (1–2 tsp) cold unsalted butter, for finishing
¼–½ tsp red wine vinegar, only if needed after tasting
Salt, only if needed after tasting
steps: If using unpeeled fresh pearl onions, briefly blanch in boiling water for 30–60 seconds, cool in ice water, trim the ends, and slip off the skins. Dry thoroughly so the onions will brown rather than steam.

Melt the 15 g butter in a wide, heavy skillet over medium heat. Add the pearl onions in a single layer and brown gently for about 8–10 minutes, turning carefully to color several sides without breaking them apart.
Stir the More Than Gourmet concentrate into 120 mL water until loosened. Pour into the skillet, add the thyme and bay leaf, and season lightly with black pepper. Do not add salt yet.

Cover and simmer very gently for about 25–40 minutes, turning occasionally, until a knife slips into the onions but they still hold their shape. Add a splash of the reserved water, or more as needed, if the pan begins to dry before the onions are tender.

Remove the lid and discard the herbs. Simmer uncovered, turning gently, until the cooking liquid concentrates into a dark, glossy glaze that coats the onions rather than pooling in the pan. Add small splashes of water if the glaze tightens before the onions are fully tender.

Remove from the heat and swirl in 5–10 g cold butter. Taste first; add ¼ tsp red wine vinegar only if the glaze needs brightness, increasing toward ½ tsp if desired. Add salt only if necessary. Serve warm.
notes: IN DEVELOPMENT: Julia Child's Oignons Glacés à Brun is the inspiration; this is a house adaptation using More Than Gourmet Demi-Glace Gold concentrate instead of plain beef stock. Concentrate is deliberately used stronger than the package's usual reconstitution ratio to produce a lacquered glaze. Keep the liquid just sufficient for a gentle braise and adjust with water as necessary. Target: intact, tender onions with a deeply savory, clingy beef glaze rather than a sweet sauce or a pool of gravy. No added sugar. Red wine vinegar is the selected acid, but taste the finished glaze before adding any. Make-ahead: braise until tender and refrigerate; rewarm with a splash of water and finish reducing, then add cold butter and any needed vinegar immediately before serving. Record actual cooking time and the amount of concentrate and vinegar used in the first test.
